entra.intro: Register an app in the Microsoft Entra admin center, then paste its details below.
entra.s1: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center (entra.microsoft.com) as at least an Application Developer.
entra.s2: Go to Entra ID › App registrations › New registration; name it and choose "Single tenant".
entra.s3: Under Redirect URI, select the "Web" platform and paste the Redirect URL shown above, then Register.
entra.s4: On the Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID. The Issuer URL is https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0.
entra.s5: Go to Certificates & secrets › New client secret and copy the secret Value (not the Secret ID).
entra.s6: Enter the client ID, client secret, and issuer URL in the fields above.
entra.s7: For group→team sync, add the Microsoft Graph GroupMember.Read.All permission under API permissions and grant admin consent.
entra.s8: For OneDrive/SharePoint document sync, add the Microsoft Graph Files.Read and Sites.Read.All permissions under API permissions and grant admin consent. If you only want sign-in, remove the two scopes from the Scopes field above.

google.intro: Create an OAuth client in the Google Cloud Console, then paste its details below.
google.s1: In the Google Cloud Console, open APIs & Services › Credentials › Create credentials › OAuth client ID.
google.s3: Under Authorized redirect URIs, add the Redirect URL shown above and save.
google.s4: Copy the Client ID and Client secret shown at the top of the client page.
google.s5: Enter them above with the Issuer URL https://accounts.google.com — the endpoints are discovered automatically.
google.groupsNote: Note: Google's standard OIDC does not return group memberships — group→team sync needs the Admin SDK / Cloud Identity API with a Workspace admin. Other OIDC providers (Okta, Auth0, Keycloak) work the same way: enter the issuer URL and client credentials.

oauth2.intro: For providers without OIDC discovery, configure the endpoints manually.
oauth2.s1: Register a web/OAuth2 application with your provider and add the Redirect URL shown above.
oauth2.s2: Copy the client ID and client secret.
oauth2.s3: Enter the authorization, token, and userinfo endpoint URLs from your provider's documentation.
oauth2.s4: If your provider uses non-standard claim names, map email/name/groups under Advanced.

saml.intro: Configure a SAML 2.0 application in your IdP, then paste its details below.
saml.s1: In your IdP, create a new SAML 2.0 application.
saml.s2: Set the ACS (Assertion Consumer Service) URL and the Entity ID / Audience to the SP values shown above, or upload the SP metadata URL.
saml.s3: Set the Name ID format to email address.
saml.s4: Copy the IdP entity ID, the IdP single sign-on URL, and the IdP signing certificate (PEM) into the fields above.
saml.s5: Map the email, name, and group attributes in your IdP; if their names differ, set the matching attribute names under Advanced.

providerOptions.providerLevelDescription:
Free-form JSON forwarded verbatim as extra request body fields to every model on this provider. The shape is dictated by the upstream API — Tale does not interpret these fields, it just passes them through.

The available knobs depend on whether the upstream is a routing gateway or a direct inference vendor:

**Gateways** aggregate multiple backends and expose routing controls:

- **OpenRouter** — routing options live under a top-level `provider` key (pick the quantization, fallback policy, allowed backends, etc.):

```json
{ "provider": { "quantizations": ["fp8"], "allow_fallbacks": false } }
```

- **Vercel AI Gateway** — primarily routes via the model-ID prefix and HTTP headers; body-level passthrough is limited to observability fields like `metadata`:

```json
{ "metadata": { "tale_agent": "support" } }
```

**Direct vendors** host their own models, so there is no routing layer and no `quantizations` field — the precision is fixed at deploy time. Their passthrough fields are model-behavior knobs at the body's top level:

- **OpenAI**:

```json
{ "service_tier": "priority", "parallel_tool_calls": false }
```

- **Together AI**:

```json
{ "safety_model": "meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B", "repetition_penalty": 1.1 }
```

Refer to each provider's API docs for the exact field names and accepted values.
providerOptions.modelLevelDescription: Free-form JSON merged on top of the provider-level defaults and forwarded as extra request body fields. The shape mirrors the upstream API and differs per provider — Tale forwards verbatim without interpretation.
providerOptions.modelLevelHelp:
Examples — gateways and direct vendors expose different kinds of knobs:

- **OpenRouter** (gateway) — pin a backend by quantization:

```json
{ "provider": { "quantizations": ["fp8"] } }
```

- **Vercel AI Gateway** (gateway) — observability tag (most routing is header- or model-prefix-based):

```json
{ "metadata": { "tale_agent": "support" } }
```

- **OpenAI** (direct) — pick an SLA tier:

```json
{ "service_tier": "priority" }
```

- **Together AI** (direct) — apply moderation:

```json
{ "safety_model": "meta-llama/Llama-Guard-4-12B" }
```

Direct vendors don't expose quantization as a request field — pick a different model ID instead. Keys like `model` / `messages` / `max_tokens` / `temperature` are rejected — set those at the agent level. Empty input clears the override.

requestBodyMap.modelLevelDescription: Rename or remove fields on the final request Tale sends to this model — for endpoints whose wire format differs. Unlike Provider Options, this never reaches the provider as data; it rewrites the body in place.
requestBodyMap.guideLabel: How the request body map works
requestBodyMap.modelLevelHelp:
Two optional keys:

- **rename** — map one field name to another (applied first). The classic case is an OpenAI/Azure reasoning deployment that wants `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`:

```json
{ "rename": { "max_tokens": "max_completion_tokens" } }
```

- **remove** — drop fields the endpoint rejects:

```json
{ "remove": ["frequency_penalty"] }
```

Models flagged with a reasoning capability already get the `max_tokens` → `max_completion_tokens` rename automatically. Empty input clears the override.
